A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PhysCtrl. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including retained material that was relocated or renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original trajectory and video evaluations, ablations, a 35-response user study, and physics-parameter estimation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds simulator controls, failure examples, and a preliminary multi-object collision experiment.

M1.justification: The trajectory architecture, conditioning variables, losses, and inverse-estimation procedure remain unchanged. Section 4.2 newly describes VGGT reconstruction and PCA-based floor-height recovery, but v1 already conditions on floor height without explaining its source. The PDFs do not establish whether this is a new pipeline component or previously undocumented implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and held-out evaluation on object–cube collisions with varying approach angles and distances (Section 6). This is a bounded extension beyond single-object dynamics; the existing four-material dataset, video evaluation, and inverse-estimation task remain.

E2.justification: New Table 4 compares PhysCtrl against traditional-simulator trajectories for video generation at two point counts. The existing video baselines, Motion2VecSets and MDM trajectory baselines, and differentiable-MPM inverse-estimation comparator are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a 2,048-versus-8,192-point simulator control and reports four-step DDIM sampling alongside the existing 25-step setting. Existing training budgets, metrics, and evaluation sample counts remain stated as before. Neither version links the revised trajectory scores to a changed sampling setting.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained attention and loss ablations, v2 adds tests of replacing learned trajectories with simulator outputs and increasing point density (Table 4). New Figure 8 also supplies trajectory and video failure cases. These substantially expand the analysis of the pipeline's necessity and failure conditions.

E5.justification: The new checklist explicitly explains that computational cost prevents repeated experiments for error bars. This adds replication-related disclosure; neither PDF supplies seed lists, confidence intervals, significance tests, or an exact repeated-run count.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 replace PhysCtrl's vIoU/CD/Corr values of 77.03%/0.0030/0.0016 with 77.59%/0.0028/0.0015 and revise every ablation row while retaining their rankings. v2 adds simulator-control scores, 93.70% collision vIoU, and four-step runtimes of 0.13/0.48 seconds for the base/large models. Existing video, user-study, and inverse-estimation results remain unchanged. The cause of the revised trajectory scores is unspecified.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, including the MPM relations, training losses, and inverse-estimation energy, are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain their meaning. The conclusion changes the scope qualification from not modeling multi-object coupling to having conducted an initial multi-object study, modestly extending the demonstrated applicability.

C2.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands the applicability discussion with thin-structure and internal-deformation failures, conflicts between physical controls and video-model priors, and occlusion hallucinations. It also attributes geometric robustness to training diversity and noise augmentation. Section 5.3 newly interprets simulator-based video quality as comparable and increased point density as unhelpful.

D1.justification: v2 documents floor-height recovery, DaS tracking-video construction through nearest-point associations, and four-step sampling runtimes. The checklist additionally promises training code, checkpoints, and dataset-generation code after acceptance. These extend reproducibility information without establishing that the resources are available.

R1.justification: v2 adds six cited works: SC-GS, MoSca, VGGT, and three audio-generation/editing papers. These support sparse-control reasoning, reconstruction details, and broader diffusion context; the principal positioning against simulators and generative-dynamics methods remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. v2 makes localized introduction and method edits, adds a Discussion section and the NeurIPS checklist, and updates affiliation and conference-header text.

P2.justification: v2 adds the simulator-comparison Table 4 and failure-case Figure 8, rearranges existing displays, and expands Figure 7's caption. The original supplementary Figure 8 becomes Figure 9, while the user-study and inverse-estimation tables are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: The simulator controls, concrete failure examples, and clearer pipeline documentation provide a limited net improvement in evidential support and transparency. Important reporting weaknesses remain: trajectory-score revisions are unexplained and lack uncertainty, and the collision experiment has sparse protocol detail. The added checklist also introduces an inconsistency by denying human-subject research despite Appendix B's retained 35-response user study.
